subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: If the curved surface of a right circular cylinder inscribed in a sphere of radius r is maximum, show that the height of the cylinder is √2 r.

mark_split.label: Relate the cylinder to the sphere
Write the curved surface in h alone

recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — say what equation the sphere gives you, what quantity you would maximise, and how you would prove the value you find is a maximum.

steps.label: Relate the cylinder to the sphere
steps.margin_note: First mark. The examiner looks for the right triangle with legs R and h/2 and hypotenuse r. Half the height, not the whole height.
lines: Let R be the radius and h the height of the cylinder inscribed in the sphere of radius r.
The axis of the cylinder passes through the centre of the sphere, so the centre lies at the mid-point of the axis.
The sphere radius to a rim point, the half-height h/2 and the cylinder radius R form a right triangle:

recall.must_convey: That the sphere gives R² + (h/2)² = r², so R² = r² − h²/4.
accept: the cylinder radius the half height and the sphere radius make a right triangle
R squared plus h by two whole squared equals r squared
use half the height in the right triangle
sphere radius tho right triangle rasta, h by two vaadali
write R squared as r squared minus h squared by four
remove R using the sphere equation

steps.why: The sphere is the constraint. It gives one equation between R and h, and without it the curved surface holds two variables and cannot be differentiated as a function of one.
common_mistakes: Writing R² + h² = r², which uses the full height instead of half of it.
Treating R as a fixed number and varying only h.
steps.memory_tip: The centre of the sphere sits half-way up the cylinder, so the vertical leg of the right triangle is h/2, never h.

steps.label: Write the curved surface in h alone
steps.margin_note: Second mark. The examiner looks for the curved surface reduced to one variable. Write one line saying why S² may replace S — because S is positive.
lines: Curved surface area of the cylinder:  S = 2πRh
S is positive, so S is greatest exactly where S² is greatest. Work with S²:

recall.must_convey: That S = 2πRh becomes a function of h alone, and that S² is maximised instead of S because S is positive.
accept: curved surface is two pi R h
substitute R from the sphere equation to get S in h only
maximise S squared because S is positive
S square maximise cheste square root pothundi
write f of h equal to four r squared h squared minus h to the fourth
reduce the surface area to one variable h

steps.why: Maximising S² instead of S removes the square root, and the two reach their greatest value at the same h because S is positive. Differentiating the root form is allowed but longer and easier to slip on.
common_mistakes: Using the total surface area 2πR(R + h) instead of the curved surface 2πRh.
Squaring only one factor when forming S².
steps.memory_tip: Curved surface is the label wrapped round a tin: 2πR times h. The two flat lids are what total surface area adds on top.

steps.label: Differentiate and solve
steps.margin_note: Third mark. The examiner looks for f′(h) = 0 solved correctly, with h = 0 discarded and a reason given for discarding it.
lines: h = 0 gives no cylinder, so it is discarded and  2r² − h² = 0
h² = 2r²   ⇒   h = √2 r      (h > 0, so the negative root is not taken)

recall.must_convey: That f′(h) = 4h(2r² − h²) = 0 gives h² = 2r², so h = √2 r, after rejecting h = 0.
accept: differentiate and set the derivative equal to zero
factor out four h and solve two r squared minus h squared equals zero
h squared is two r squared so h is root two r
h equal to zero reject cheyyali, cylinder undadu
take only the positive root because h is a length
the stationary point is at root two r

steps.why: Factorising before solving shows both roots on one line, and h = 0 is discarded because a cylinder of zero height has no curved surface at all.
common_mistakes: Taking the negative root h = −√2 r, which cannot be a length.
steps.memory_tip: Take the common factor h out first. A stationary-point equation that factors hands you the rejected root and the real root in the same line.

steps.label: Confirm the maximum and conclude
steps.margin_note: Fourth mark, and the one most students lose. Write f″, put h² = 2r² into it, and state the sign. A stationary point is not a maximum until the test says so.
lines: A negative second derivative means the stationary point is a maximum.
So f is maximum at h = √2 r, and therefore S is maximum at h = √2 r.

lines.text: ∴ the curved surface is maximum when the height of the cylinder is h = √2 r

recall.must_convey: That f″ = 8r² − 12h² is negative at h² = 2r², which proves the value is a maximum, so h = √2 r.
accept: second derivative is negative so it is a maximum
f double dash equals minus sixteen r squared which is less than zero
apply the second derivative test before writing the answer
second derivative negative unte maximum
the height is root two times r
confirm it is a maximum and not a minimum

steps.why: Setting the derivative to zero only finds where the rate of change stops. It could be a maximum, a minimum or neither, so the second derivative test is a separate step and carries its own mark.
common_mistakes: Stopping at f′(h) = 0 and calling the value a maximum with no test.
Substituting h = √2 r into f′ instead of f″.
steps.memory_tip: Second derivative negative means the curve bends downward there, so the stationary point is a maximum. Positive means it bends upward, so it is a minimum.

insider_note: The sphere's centre bisects the axis, so R² + (h/2)² = r² eliminates R. Maximising then gives h = r√2, and squaring to avoid the root keeps the algebra clean.
